title: What do you think about a character generator in this graphic style?

posts.author: Ombladje
posts.body:
Hello!
I am thinking about creating a character generator in the graphic style of the character in the image I marked. The character has a different camera perspective and a different color tone. In the end, there should be up to 400 individual graphics for the generator.
All characters should be in a European medieval/fantasy style. There should be many with simple clothing or armor. There will only be character sprites, no faces. There will be only one walking animation, no other animations. Only female and male characters will be included, no grandfathers or children. Colors can be manually changed for all individual parts.
I would like to offer the generator for free, but with the option to purchase additional graphics for it.
What do you think of the idea? Please be honest. I am very interested in the community’s opinion because this is meant for the community. If something about the character doesn’t fit, feel free to say so, I can make changes.
Looking forward to your comments! It would help me a lot

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Personally I'm not a fan of the style or the angle, but I think the real problem is all of this:
Ombladje said:
There will only be character sprites, no faces. There will be only one walking animation, no other animations. Only female and male characters will be included, no grandfathers or children.
Click to expand...
While I'm sure there are people who will appreciate yet another free tool, personally I would say this isn't good enough. You're basically just getting less content than the default assets only to change up the style a tiny bit.
The angle also doesn't go with any existing tilesets, so I'm really not seeing the target audience for this.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
With faces, I would be interested. Faces are the main way for players to visualise the actors. They are very important for menus that include selecting an actor, for instance the main menu where you might, for example, choose which party member to equip a new weapon or piece of armour.
While I don't go for side-view battles, a lot of RPG Maker users do, so if you want the character generator to be popular, you would be wise to cater for side-view battlers as well.
Children are useful as characters to be rescued, but aren't really necessary for my games. (It can be a bit repetitive to rescue damsel-in-distress after damsel-in-distress, and it is also nice to have characters without NSW potential for a change.) However, some people might be making games more focused on kids.
I use character generators quite a bit (MV for humans, MZ for elves and goblins, increasingly Schlangan's as I get used to it). If I could make characters look closer to people of Medieval Europe rather than Japan, I would be very happy.
I use a plugin to convert the default Chibli sprites to make them a little taller (currently the OcRam one). My older games used 56 pixel high walking sprites but I currently use 64 pixel high sprites. The tile-sets I use have doors 2 tiles high, so taller sprites look right to me.
Just a suggestion, would it be easier for you to just do a replacement set of character generator parts? The Schlangan generator gives you the choice of multiple sets (for instance, MV or MZ).
Here are some examples of sprites that were done in either the [
EDITED to say MV]
MV or Schlangan generator, made 64 pixels high by the OcRam plugin:
Second Edit
: The clothes on those sprites look more early modern or modern to me than medieval.
Not sure when trousers became common for men in Western Europe. I know that in the 17th Century (1601 to 1700) knee-britches were expected for middle and upper class males. Trousers were used by the labouring classes.
Are you sure about the jackets? To me they look late 19th, 20th or 21st Centuries. I am not an expert in historical costume so I may be wrong, and am open to be corrected.
Hats for men outside were pretty much required until the late 20th Century. I remember getting in trouble at school during the 1960s for not wearing my cap whilst walking back from school. The type of hat also expressed social status.

I know some people that might be interested in these, but the first image doesn't or doesn't seem to work as well as the second image's style, and to be honest looks even harder to animate with the way the limbs look.
the second image has depth, by that I mean it looks more tri dimensional, you can easily see which parts of the clothes are thicker and closer to the camera, for example you can easily see that the pink witch is wearing a small white cloak on top of her tress, the head is closer to the front, the sprite also makes it easy to point the knees, and both legs face forward so it's easier to animate the walk.
The first one though looks too flat, kinda like a piece of paper, you can still divide the shirt from the jacket, but it doesn't shake off the feeling of it being a bit too flat, the head works very well but you don't usually animate that aside maybe the hair, the arms I guess might be alright to animate, but the legs, it's kinda hard to see where the knees are, also the legs face opposite directions, it looks like a hassle to animate consistently on different characters.
Unless you use more than the classic 3 frames for walk animation that usually include the still character, I don't think it'll look good to be honest.
​
@Ombladje
If I can ask, was the sprite made from a template, or was it made with the cloths on from the very start? cause if that's the case, you should try making a naked template so that you can easily fix certain parts, and shade it in a way that makes it less flat.
Edit: sorry for the various edits, messed up with the multi quotes
